questions.question: At 120 requests/s, 1,200 input tokens per request, and 320 output tokens per request, what is the raw token rate?
options: 144,000 tokens/s
182,400 tokens/s
38,400 tokens/s
1,520 tokens/s
questions.explanation: Each request carries 1,520 total tokens, so 120 x 1,520 = 182,400 raw tokens/s. Input and output still have different serving and price behavior.

questions.question: Why does the capacity lab keep raw tokens separate from weighted serving units?
options: Raw token counts cannot be measured
Only input tokens use accelerators
Model tier and prompt-versus-decode work change how token volume consumes worker capacity
Weighted units guarantee response quality
questions.explanation: Raw tokens describe demand. Weighted units are an explicit planning assumption for how a selected tier processes input and generated tokens.

questions.question: What is the safe behavior when a required input-safety decision is unavailable?
options: Route affected work to a restricted response path and keep risky generation and tools disabled
Bypass the policy service to protect latency
Send the request directly to the largest model
Retry without a deadline until the dependency returns
questions.explanation: A missing required policy decision is not permission. Restricted deterministic behavior preserves the safety boundary and makes the degradation observable.

questions.question: Why is a conversation summary not an authoritative user record?
options: It always contains every prior token
It is stored inside model weights after each turn
It cannot reduce prompt length
It is compressed model-generated context that can omit or distort details
questions.explanation: A summary lowers context cost but remains fallible. Permissions, account settings, and mutable facts belong in authoritative systems accessed through controlled tools.

questions.question: A side-effecting tool times out after receiving a request. What prevents a retry from duplicating the action?
options: A larger model tier
A stable idempotency key enforced by the tool boundary
A longer conversation summary
A second unbounded retry loop
questions.explanation: The caller cannot know whether a timed-out side effect completed. Reusing an idempotency key lets the provider return the original result or suppress a duplicate action.

questions.question: Which metric set best explains a slow first token?
options: Only average generated tokens per second
Only daily active users
Admission, policy, context load, queue, and prefill latency under one request ID
Only model-training loss
questions.explanation: Time to first token accumulates before decode streaming begins. Stage-level latency under one request ID identifies whether admission, policy, storage, queueing, or prefill caused the delay.
